bull_bear.body: Prioritizing working capital for new project execution; no dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on debt reduction and margin recovery
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: High dependence on subcontracting eroding margins; delays in project commencement; cost inflation (materials, labor); regulatory delays in Sri Lanka project; concentration risk in few large clients
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Despite declining profits, order book grew 66% YoY — indicating strong pipeline; the drop in PAT is structural (mix shift), not operational failure; auditor’s report is clean despite financial stress
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Infrastructure: ₹2096.26cr (9 projects); Buildings: ₹8.03cr (1 project); Water management: ₹365.85cr (1 project); Total new awards FY26: ₹2470.14cr
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- The deck describes a contractor whose current order book "as on date consists of 39 projects with outstanding value of ₹3750.83 crores worth of work remaining to be executed as on date", which management frames as the base for "growth trajectory for the current and upcoming financial years".
- Order intake is concentrated in infrastructure: of the 11 new projects worth ₹2470.14 crores awarded "during the period up to March 2026", Infrastructure accounts for ₹2096.26 crores across 9 projects, Water management ₹365.85 crores across 1 project and Buildings ₹8.03 crores across 1 project.
- Management states it is "actively monitoring and participating in more construction projects and are expecting more positive outcome in the upcoming financial year".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Auditor] The deck includes an auditor's-report slide stating that "The outcome of the review conducted does not have any negative or adverse remarks against the standalone and consolidated financial results of the company."
- [Guidance tone] Management expects "the profit of next quarter will be better but significant revenue contribution is expected only from Q2 of next financial year."
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin fell to 7.33% (from 14.20% in FY25); EBITDA margin at 2.36% (from 7.48%); driven by higher subcontracting, material/fuel/labor inflation, and non-recurring project losses
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Management expects improved profitability from Q2FY27 as newly awarded self-executed projects (including BHEL-related) begin revenue contribution; focus on increasing own-execution volume and cost control.
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body: ₹3750.83cr outstanding (as of Mar 2026), including ₹2470.14cr newly awarded in FY26 (9 infrastructure, 1 building, 1 water project)
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into Sri Lanka (piling approved, building permit pending); potential to capture more public infrastructure tenders in India; scaling self-execution model to improve margins
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: R.P.P Infra is a mid-sized EPC player with a robust ₹3,750cr order book, but faces severe margin compression due to shift from self-executed to subcontracted projects and rising input costs. Recovery is expected from Q2FY27 as new self-executed projects ramp up, though near-term profitability remains under pressure.

rows.quant: Rs 205.89 cr order LOST; ~72.6% of mcap
rows.text: loses its **Rs 205.89 crore Global Sports City work order**, terminated by the Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu, which is redesigning the project. The company had begun work and incurred substantial expenditure
